requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark.
The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.

In case an ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall either have an approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, or be demonstrated by a test report from a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority to be not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband electromagnetic interference value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

For the stripline method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).

For the TEM cell method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).

For the BCI method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).

For the ALSE method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).

For the reverberation chamber method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a).

For the stripline method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).

For the TEM cell method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).

For the BCI method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).

For the ALSE method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 8 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).

For the reverberation chamber method according to Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 6 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the ESA representative of the type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The ESA shall be tested for starting profile according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the ESA for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile, the ESA shall be tested at immunity test level II for 12 V systems and II for 24 V systems with 10 pulses, meeting functional status B for ESA related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA related to immunity related functions, and D for ESA not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall withstand an immunity test level of -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses, meeting FPSC III for functions related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall withstand an immunity test level of +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses, meeting FPSC I for functions related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall withstand an immunity test level of +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems for 10 pulses, meeting FPSC II for functions related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall withstand an immunity test level of -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, meeting FPSC I for functions related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall withstand an immunity test level of +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, meeting FPSC I for functions related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The starting profile test shall only be applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.

ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
The ESA under test for broadband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The radiated broadband emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The ESA shall be tested for narrowband electromagnetic emissions according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.

The ESA narrowband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

ESAs other than those involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 or reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA immunity test in the TEM cell shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.

The ESA bulk current injection immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench using either the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA or the BCI closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
The ESA stripline immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
The ESA reverberation chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be subjected to immunity testing with test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be subjected to immunity testing with the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
A separate approval shall be obtained for each lamp listed in the scope of UN R148.

Where two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in UN R148 or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps with reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall, in the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
Lamps with an electronic light source control gear shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed.
In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the approval mark on the module and the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used shall both be from the same applicant.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
An electronic light source control gear being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number.
An electronic light source control gear being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
A variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number.
A variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
The approval marking shall in any case be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.

The category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall in any case be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on the detachable lens.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.2. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.3. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.4. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (b) shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations and a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number is affixed, this marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps only provided that the conditions of the following sub-paragraphs are met.

Where a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R148.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function), only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components shall be incorporated and all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation shall be fulfilled.

Where a logo is incorporated inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function), irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed.

Where a logo is incorporated inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function), the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.

Where a logo is incorporated inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function), notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 (with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated), or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, with the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source(s) holder shall conform to the holder data sheet of IEC Publication 60061 relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions, the lamp shall meet the photometric requirements for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The intensity of light emitted by the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.

Where the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No. 48, the maximum intensity of the lamp in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd, which may be verified taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the luminous intensity requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

Where a variable intensity control is used for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp under night-time conditions.

Where a variable intensity control is used for other systems, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp under standard conditions (good visibility, meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m defined according to WMO, Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation, Sixth Edition, ISBN: 92-63-16008-2, pp 1.9.1/1.9.11, Geneva 1996, and clean lens).

If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.

If one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the luminous intensity values considered for the 5:1 ratio shall be those obtained with all sources in operation.
The luminous intensities of the lamp shall comply with the requirements when tested according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall comply with the requirements inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, checked using the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall comply for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp (R1, R2, MR) or rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.

For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The rear position lamp (R1, R2, MR) or rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 4.
The rear position lamp and rear end-outline marker lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp and rear end-outline marker lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied at that angle.
Where type approval of the reversing lamp is granted with photometric verification only up to 30° inwards, the device shall only be installed in a pair.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

Unless specified otherwise, the luminous intensity of the lamp in the various directions of measurement shall be at least the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.

Where front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS, or side marker lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity of the lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

For reversing lamps, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.

Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in the standard light distribution of Annex 3 paragraph 2.1 as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8.

The reversing lamp shall meet the minimum intensities of the light emitted at the measuring points, expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, given in the standard light distribution for reversing lamps of Annex 3 paragraph 2.5.
The lamp shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.
The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C.

For the heat resistance test, the lamp shall be operated with a light source of the category specified for the lamp, supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the heat resistance test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5. of this Regulation.
Where only the maximum power is specified, the lamp shall withstand the heat resistance test with the voltage regulated to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power.
The specified average or maximum power for the heat resistance test shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of this Regulation shall be applied.

In the case of light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the heat resistance test of the lamp shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
After the lamp has been subjected to the heat resistance test and stabilized at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt, the intensity of light of the lamp measured according to paragraph 5. after the heat resistance test shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps other than reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be complied with at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
The approval number assigned to the approved type shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.

Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in UN R150.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
The trade name or mark of the applicant shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
Where required, the "TOP" marking shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations and a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed, that marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps only provided that the conditions of UN R150 paragraph 3.3.6.1. are met.

The size of the components of a single approval mark for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps in retro-reflective devices shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Retro-reflectors approved under UN Regulation No. 150 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which it is intended to be installed, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical units and filters of retro-reflectors shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of a white, red or amber retro-reflective device, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

The retro-reflector samples shall, after the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6, meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The retro-reflector shall satisfactorily withstand the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6 and then the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7.
The retro-reflector shall, if necessary, withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 and then the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device of Part 5 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall withstand the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective devices of Part 3 of Annex 4.
The retro-reflector shall withstand the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6.

The retro-reflectors in each group shall, after undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1., have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

Where more than one or a range of different axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements with reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.

For photometric measurements of Class IA or IB retro-reflectors, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

The illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector considered for photometric measurements shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.

The RI values for red Class IA and Class IB retro-reflectors, when measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the minimum RI values of retro-reflection shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP", when rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5 of UN R150, and an angle of divergence of 20', shall have a minimum RI that conforms to the value specified in paragraph 5 of UN R150.

Where a retro-reflective device is marked "TOP", with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of the Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', the RI of the retro-reflective device shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during rotation about its axis by ±5°.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the retro-reflective device shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA and IIIB, from an observation distance of 10 metres.

Moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangles of type 1 shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.

Retro-reflective devices, whether part of a lamp or not, shall withstand, stripped of all removable parts, immersion for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface of the water, repeated after turning the device through 180° so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water, followed immediately by immersion in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water at the reflecting surface after the water penetration test, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
All drain holes and other openings of the retro-reflective device shall remain open during the water spray test.
Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the retro-reflective device during the water spray test.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The retro-reflector device shall be subjected to a water spray test lasting 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).

After the water spray test and drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the retro-reflector device, nor shall one be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
After the water spray test, the RI of the retro-reflector device shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4.

Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, as verified by the corrosion resistance test described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the device shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after the corrosion test and a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Retro-reflective devices shall withstand exposure in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.

The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular the illuminating surface, after being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol, shall not show any apparent surface changes when inspected visually after about five minutes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation after its outer surface, and in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes.

The light emitted from a device required to be "white" shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) (CIE Publication 15.2, 1986, CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer) inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries W12 green boundary y = 0.150 + 0.640 x, W23 yellowish green boundary y = 0.440, W34 yellow boundary x = 0.500, W45 reddish purple boundary y = 0.382, W56 purple boundary y = 0.050 + 0.750 x and W61 blue boundary x = 0.310, with intersection points W1 (0.310, 0.348), W2 (0.453, 0.440), W3 (0.500, 0.440), W4 (0.500, 0.382), W5 (0.443, 0.382) and W6 (0.310, 0.283).

The light emitted from a device required to be "red" shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line (its linear extension across the purple range of colours between the red and the blue extremities of the spectral locus) and R41 purple boundary y = 0.980 – x, with intersection points R1 (0.645, 0.335), R2 (0.665, 0.335), R3 (0.735, 0.265) and R4 (0.721, 0.259).

The night-time light retro-reflected from a device required to be "red", excluding retro-reflective tires according to UN Regulation No. 88, shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line and R41 purple boundary y = 0.978 - x, with intersection points R1 (0.643, 0.335), R2 (0.665, 0.335), R3 (0.735, 0.265) and R4 (0.720, 0.258).

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The reference axis of signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall comply when the vehicle is unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the general installation requirements for lamps shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Lamps that are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another shall fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
The maximum height of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Where the photometric characteristics of a lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

The luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable, in case of doubt.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light reflected by the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
Where any lamp is installed on movable components, the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. of UN R48 shall be fulfilled.

Where additional lamps for the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position (stable or natural rest position(s) specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not) different from the "normal position of use", unless this is not practicable and the alternative provisions are met.

If it is not practicable to keep the apparent surface of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors hidden no more than 50 per cent by a movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for these lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is used, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is used, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

Where rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Where rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.

For rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except that no account is taken of obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

Where the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

All lamps (devices) installed on a vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48.
Light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle approved according to UN Regulation No. 48 and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only, this requirement not concerning light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources except for when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
The number of reversing lamps on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm shall be one device mandatory and a second device optional.
The reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be installed not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground in height.

The reversing lamp shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle in length, except that, if installed, the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. may be fitted on the side of the vehicle provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. are fulfilled.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The number of stop lamps shall be two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device on all categories of vehicles.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For all other categories of vehicles than M1 and N1, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the distance in between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be installed above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm in height, or 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.

If optional S1 or S2 category stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The geometric visibility horizontal angle of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility vertical angle of S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

For the rear position lamp, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for the optional rear lamps.

For all vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear position lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The rear position lamp shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

If the optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable width requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1., the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility horizontal angle of the rear position lamp shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The geometric visibility vertical angle of the rear position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where the rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward geometric visibility angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility horizontal angle of the rear position lamp shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative with a rear side-marker lamp installed, the geometric visibility vertical angle of the rear position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative, the rear position lamp shall, to be considered visible, provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
A closed-circuit tell-tale shall be mandatory for the rear position lamps, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The rear position lamp tell-tale shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.

For the rear retro-reflector, the point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For all vehicle categories other than M1 and N1, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm, or not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), or not more than 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be 30° inwards and outwards in the horizontal angle.

The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be 10° above and below horizontal in the vertical angle, except that where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

The rear position lamps shall be switched ON when daytime running lamps are switched ON, except that the rear position lamps and the other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON and may remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
The emergency stop signal shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the hazard warning signal is activated.

In the case where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and "7b" is the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2., function F1 shall not be transparent to function F2 for the reciprocal incorporation of two functions.

The zones 1 and 2 used for assessing the visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

The zones 1 and 2 used for assessing the visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width, with the foremost point of contact corresponding to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane if there are several points of contact.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6., in width, in height and in length shall comply with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of UN R48.
The measured distances of the position of lamps shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The angles of geometric visibility of each lamp, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall comply with paragraph 5.10. of UN R48.

Every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle and the tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp when switched on.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
